newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hizbollah says it raids Israeli force in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Hizbollah says it raids Israeli force in Lebanon.

text.p: Lebanon's Hizbollah said its fighters waged two attacks against Israeli forces in south Lebanon on Sunday, causing casualties and damage.

The pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) said in a statement in Beirut its fighters opened fire twice at an armoured force in Basseel area in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, "inflicting a number of casualties, dead and wounded".
There was no immediate independent confirmation.

The group said two Mirkava tanks were destroyed in the assaults which came as Hizbollah members and supporters held a rally in Beirut to mark "Martyr's Day" commemorating fallen guerrillas killed in confrontations with Israeli forces.

On Saturday, Hizbollah guerrillas killed one Israeli soldier and wounded two when they opened machinegun and anti-tank rocket fire at an Israeli post at Blat in the western sector of the occupation zone.
Hizbollah opposes Arab-Israeli peace talks and leads a guerrilla war in a bid to oust Israeli and allied militia forces from the 15-km (nine-mile) deep zone in south Lebanon.
Some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong allied militia patrols the zone set up in 1985 to deter cross-border guerrilla raids on northern Israel.
